meta.audit: CWVWWF data audit — v6 (delta audit of 3c43e7b + application of high-confidence corrections)

new_commits_audited.subject: Constrain generated talent and improve AI scouting

two_parts: Part 1 — delta audit of 3c43e7b against the v5 findings.

Part 2 — application of the high-confidence wrestler, free-agent and arrival-date corrections from the committed research (audit/cwvwwf_patch_recommendations.json, 133 ops @ 12d9fcd; data.js/timeline.js unchanged since, so the ops still mapped cleanly). Applied as local commit 7621cf2 in the WCW-vs-WWF clone and published as audit/cwvwwf_high_confidence_corrections.patch (push to the game repo was blocked by token permissions — see delivery).

summary.part1: 3c43e7b fixes 3 of the v5 findings outright (NEW-1 bias, NEW-2 no-compete bypass, FA-ENG-3 historical mode); the female-name fix is broken (NEW-9); 11 findings remain open.
summary.part2: 92 correction operations applied to js/data.js (+2 test assertion updates) as local commit 7621cf2 / published patch; 6 documented deviations, all engine-necessity or turn-formula corrections.
summary.model: Pre-correction: 408 = 311+60+37 verified again. Post-correction baseline: 387 = 290+60+37 at t0, 43 dated FA arrivals, 430 workers ever by 2001. Both test suites green; determinism preserved.

part1_fix_verification.evidence: isIndy cold threshold lowered to 28 normal / 24 hard / 32 easy (was 38/32/38) and the gender bonus (+30 WWF/+15 WCW) deleted from the shared cold path. Measured: t1 WCW signed 12 indies — 10 male (9 ordinary), 2 female, 1 gem. Through t300: 37/39/37 of 150 signed on normal (ordinary men 26/31/30, women 5/1/5) and 79/150 on hard. Recruitment now tracks the stat distribution instead of gender.
part1_fix_verification.note: The bonus removal also affects HISTORICAL female FAs in the shared cold path (marginal women no longer clear the 55/48 thresholds) — a deliberate scope-broadening beyond generated talent, flagged as an observation.

part1_fix_verification.evidence: The cold path now calls canSign() before scoring ('const ncCold = canSign(state, w, comp); if (!ncCold.ok) continue;'). Repeated the v5 steal test: a written-released indy with a 16-week no-compete was NOT signed by the rival through the whole window.

New state.game.generatedTalentMode ('historical' when indyPool=0, else 'full') gates BOTH the January indy class and the rookie training class, plus a state.game.talentIntake ledger. indyPool=0 game: 348 wrestlers at t0 (37 jobbers remain), and after 110 weeks: 0 rookies, 0 indy classes, empty ledger. Old saves (no mode field) keep classes running — backwards compatible.

part1_fix_verification.status: ATTEMPTED, STILL BROKEN → superseded by NEW-9
part1_fix_verification.evidence: 3c43e7b adds a 26-name FEMALE_FIRST_NAMES pool and a gender parameter to makeName — but the else branch unconditionally overwrites first with a ROOKIE_FIRST_NAMES pick, discarding the female name (see NEW-9).

part1_new_findings.category: Female generated workers still get male names
part1_new_findings.current_value: js/engine.js makeName(): `if (gender === 'f' && !flavor) first = pick(FEMALE_FIRST_NAMES);` is followed by a SEPARATE `if (!first && flavor && ...) {...} else { first = pick(ROOKIE_FIRST_NAMES); last = pick(ROOKIE_LAST_NAMES); }` — the else reassigns first unconditionally, so the female pick is drawn and immediately discarded (and one extra rng call is consumed per female worker). Female international workers are exempt by design (!flavor guard) and keep drawing from the male INTL pools.
part1_new_findings.recommended_value: Change the else to `else if (!first) { first = pick(ROOKIE_FIRST_NAMES); ... }` (or restructure so the female pick short-circuits).
part1_new_findings.explanation: Verified empirically at 3c43e7b: 0 of 12 female indies in a fresh game have female first names ('Drew Bradley [f]', 'Ian Wright [f]', …); 0 female-named workers among all AI indy signings across four 300-week runs; all 5 AJW female jobbers male-named (intl exemption).
part1_new_findings.source: Code js/engine.js L272-286; empirical generator runs at 3c43e7b (this audit)

part2_deviations.what: Eddy Guerrero applied as an ECW FA arrival at t13 instead of the literal op {company: null, contract: 21}.
part2_deviations.why: WRESTLERS entries with company:null are unsignable decoration in the current engine: newGame hardcodes faUntil:null/asking:null for starters, the AI allFAs filter excludes non-indy faUntil-null workers, and the FA tab hides pop<20 non-notable rows. The research itself specifies 'ECW arrival ~turn 13 (April 8, 1995)', which the FA_ARRIVALS mechanism delivers cleanly (16-week window, ECW interest).

part2_deviations.what: Hardy Boyz applied as WWF FA arrivals at t144 instead of 'seeded unsigned free agents at start'.
part2_deviations.why: Same engine limitation as DEV-1 — seeded starters with company:null cannot be signed by anyone. The t144 arrival (mid-1998, interest WWF) is the historically load-bearing event and is fully playable. Jeff's age set to 20 and Matt's to 23 (arrival-date ages; the research's 17/20 were framed for a Jan-1995 seed and the engine has no aging mechanic).

part2_deviations.what: Rick Rude's arrival turn corrected from the research's '~96' to t90.
part2_deviations.why: The research note is internally inconsistent: t96 is January 1997 by the game's turn formula (year=1995+⌊t/48⌋, month=⌊t/4⌋%12), while the sourced date is November 1996 (= t88-91). Per the standing 'never hand-derive turns' rule the DATE wins; t90 = November wk3 1996 (November to Remember, Nov 16).

part2_deviations.what: Kurasawa (t36), Rad Radford (t18) and Phineas Godwinn (t30, age 26) were re-added as dated FA arrivals alongside their removals from the start.
part2_deviations.why: Their High-confidence recommendations explicitly include the later arrival ('add a WCW signing event ~turn 36', 'WWF debut May 13, 1995', 'the Godwinns debuted on WWF TV in August 1995, age 26'), and Phineas's absence would permanently break the Godwinns team. The nine 'optionally add…' removals (barbarian, barry-windham, jim-neidhart, tom-brandi, missy-hyatt, the-shark/savio-vega rename chains, louie-spicolli) were applied as removals only, exactly as the ops list carries them.

part2_deviations.what: Mark Henry's finisher entered as 'Press Slam' (not 'World's Strongest Slam').
part2_deviations.why: Single-quoted JS string safety (apostrophe) plus period accuracy — the World's Strongest Slam name postdates 1996.

part2_deviations.what: Two test/sim.js assertions updated to the corrected data.
part2_deviations.why: 'betrayal flip' assumed Hogan starts heel (he now correctly starts face; the test now asserts the align actually flips, direction-agnostic) and the custom-fed draft pick list included eddy-guerrero (now an FA arrival; replaced with chris-benoit, keeping the roster size at 8).
